item.title: Southern Pottery Is Sensational At Cagle
item.description: ATHENS, GA. — On January 24, Cagle Auction Company conducted its 256-lot Southern Pottery & Folk Art Auction. The sale sold 98 percent by lot and totaled just under $121,000. The post Southern Pottery Is Sensational At Cagle first appeared on Antiques And The Arts Weekly.

item.title: Americana Drives Sotheby’s Antiques Week Auctions
item.description: NEW YORK CITY — Sotheby’s billed a grouping of its Antiques Week sales as Visions of America, bringing together sublime examples evincing American craftsmanship and ingenuity, ranging from furniture to important historical documents dating back 250 years when the United States was establishing itself as a nation. The post Americana Drives Sotheby’s Antiques Week Auctions first appeared on Antiques And The Arts Weekly.

item.title: Morse Landscapes Earn First Prize At Stair
item.description: HUDSON, N.Y. — Two oil on board paintings by Samuel F.B. Morse (1791-1872) achieved top-lot status at Stair Galleries’ January 29 Americana auction. “A View of Cazenovia Lake” (shown) and “View of Parapet Fall At Trenton” went well past their $3/5,000 estimate to sell for $65,500, including buyer’s premium. item.title: Tennessee Redware Jar Tops Crocker Farm
item.description: SPARKS, MD. — A rare Tennessee redware jar, attributed to C.A. Haun Pottery, Greene County, having crosshatched copper slip, outperformed its $15/25,000 estimate to attain $108,000, including buyer’s premium, at Crocker Farm’s winter auction of the Carole Wahler collection that ran January 21-31. item.title: Clars Starts The New Year Strong With Gallery Auction
item.description: OAKLAND, CALIF. — Furniture, decorative arts, fine art, jewelry and Asian art made up the 645 lots of Clars Auctions’ January Gallery Auction, which was conducted on the 23rd. While a sale total was not disclosed, press representative Talesa Eugenio shared that the sell-through rate was 83 percent.
